summary: Mohammad Ashraf Dar is an indologist and historian-archaeologist. He completed a Master of Philosophy at Vikram University, where he also served as a research scholar.

Mohan G. Dhadphale is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He served as a Professor at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth and was Editor of Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute in 2002.

Mona Schrempf is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who earned her doctorate in anthropology at the Free University of Berlin (~1996–2001). She taught part-time at Heidelberg University and was a research fellow at Humboldt University of Berlin (~2005–2011).

Monica Esposito was a sinologist and religious studies scholar. She studied at Ca' Foscari University of Venice (~1982–1987) and Paris Diderot University (~1988–1993), later serving as an Associate Professor at Kyoto University (~2003–2011).

Monier Monier-Williams was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Horace Hayman Wilson at Oxford. He taught at East India Company College (~1844–1858) and Cheltenham College (~1858–1860), then served as Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit (1860–1899).

Monika Horstmann is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She held posts at the University of Bonn, the Australian National University, the University of Cologne, and served as Professor of Modern South Asian Studies at Heidelberg University (~1992–2007).

Monika Zin, an Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology scholar, studied at Jagiellonian University and LMU Munich. She was a Professor at LMU Munich (~1994–2016) and the Free University of Berlin (~2016–2017), joining the Saxon Academy in 2016.

Moriichi Yamazaki is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Cambridge under Kenneth Roy Norman (~1982–1984). He held posts at Rissho University, Sendai College, and served as president of Hosen Gakuen College.

Moritz Abraham Stern was a linguist and mathematician who studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Göttingen, where he studied under Carl Friedrich Gauss in 1829. He served on the faculty at the University of Göttingen from 1830 to 1884.
Moritz Wilhelm Drobisch was a philosopher. After studying at Leipzig University from 1820 to 1824, he held an academic post there from 1826 until 1886.
Moriz Haupt was a linguist who studied at Leipzig University under Gottfried Hermann (~1826–1831). He held positions at Leipzig University (~1837–1851) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1853–1874).

Moriz Winternitz was an Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna under Georg Bühler and under Friedrich Max Müller. He served as professor at the German University in Prague from 1902 and visited Visva-Bharati University (1922–1923).

Morten Schlütter is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar. He studied at the University of Copenhagen, Komazawa University, and Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. He held academic posts at Yale, Victoria University of Wellington, UW–Madison, UCLA, and the University of Iowa.

Mortimer Wheeler was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at University College London (~1907–1912). He held posts at Amgueddfa Cymru, the London Museum, the UCL Institute of Archaeology, and served as Director-General of Archæology in India (~1944–1948).

Morton Klass was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University (1955–1959). He served at Bennington College (1959), Barnard College (1965), and Columbia University (1982–1985).

Moses Gaster was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the Jewish Theological Seminary of Breslau and Leipzig University, later holding posts at the University of Oxford (~1886–1891) and serving as President of the Folklore Society in 1909.
Mother Sayamagyi was a Buddhist and religious studies practitioner and teacher. She studied as a disciple under Sayagyi U Ba Khin from ~1953 to 1971 and later succeeded him.

Motohiro Yoritomi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Gadjin Nagao and Yuichi Kajiyama at Kyoto University, completing his PhD by 1988. He served as a professor at Shuchiin University (~1975–2010).

Motoi Ono is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tsukuba under Yasunori Ejima and earned a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna, becoming an associate professor at Tsukuba around 1994.
Motoichi Miyamoto is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1967 to 1977 and later served as an assistant professor at Kokugakuin University.
